tensions.claim: matched-regime benchmarks report opposite method orderings depending on whether the dropout simulation is MAR or expression-coupled MNAR (E2 vs E3)

mechanism_hypotheses.hypothesis: graph-smooth's advantage is MAR-specific: smoothing borrows information whose missingness pattern violates the MAR assumption it was tuned under
alternative_explanations: the two benchmarks differ in cell-type composition, not in missingness mechanism

predictions: graph-smooth's RMSE advantage disappears monotonically as the MNAR coupling strength increases, while model-based methods degrade slower
tensions.discriminating_experiment: Simulate dropout with a coupling parameter interpolating MAR→MNAR on the SAME count matrix and cell-type composition; compare both methods at each coupling strength. If the ordering flips within the interpolated range, mechanism 1 is supported; if the ordering is stable but absolute errors shift, the composition/preprocessing explanations gain support.
falsification_criteria: graph-smooth retains its advantage at maximum MNAR coupling
the flip reproduces when cell-type composition is held fixed and only normalization differs
tensions.impact_if_true: imputation benchmarks without an explicit MNAR arm cannot rank methods for real 10x data; evaluation-design contribution
tensions.impact_if_false: ordering differences are benchmark artifacts of composition/preprocessing; methods guidance unchanged
nearest_related_work: MNAR-aware simulation studies in single-cell (search: 'imputation MNAR evaluation', 2023-2025)
tensions.confidence_rationale: both orderings directly reported (direct evidence on each side); mechanism consistent with M1's own stated assumption; composition alternative not yet excluded
